messages:
kari: Heads-up: tonight's change window at 02:00 UTC. Plan: add `normalized_amount` column to transactions (INT) with out-of-band backfill. Avoid table rewrite by using nullable col + background backfill. Pin service version to release-2026-03-01 during rollout.
jin: agreed. Backfill job will be chunked by created_at, workers=4, rate=100/sec. We'll run a canary on shard db-a first.
dba-bot: Preflight checks: replicas healthy, bloat < 8%, autovacuum active. Suggested SQL sequence: ```ALTER TABLE transactions ADD COLUMN normalized_amount INT; -- nullable
-- backfill worker will run: UPDATE transactions SET normalized_amount = floor(amount_cents/100) WHERE normalized_amount IS NULL AND created_at >= $start AND created_at < $end;```
deploybot: Canary scheduled: backfill-runner v2.0 on db-a. holdpoint after first 500 rows. monitoring hooks attached.
ops-bot: baseline pulled: p50 write 20ms, p95 write 150ms, long-running queries >5s: 0.
kari: launching canary now. Call out any spikes, especially read replicas throwing read-only errors or long VACUUM waits.
deploybot: Canary progressed: 500 rows updated, no errors. moving to chunked backfill of 5k rows at 100/s.
# ~3 minutes later~
jin: saw a surge in long-running analytic queries (reporting cluster) that hit the primary replica and caused temp file growth; not sure if our backfill amplified it.
dba-bot: Observed temp_files increasing on primary; one worker spilled to disk during a simultaneous large aggregate. Not seeing locks >1s on transactions table.
ops-bot: replica lag db-a-replica at 9s (watch threshold 10s). disk i/o iowait trending up to 25%.
kari: holdpoint 1: pause backfill. @deploybot pause backfill-runner canary.
deploybot: Action: pausing canary jobs. Checkpoint saved id=chk_1709993400.
jin: can we retry at lower concurrency: workers=2 and rate=30/s? also add a pre-scan to avoid hot time ranges.
ari?: (typo)
kari: yes retry with slower config and add a short drain window for nightly report jobs. Pin remains release-2026-03-01 for the moment.
deploybot: Resuming backfill with workers=2 rate=30/s. Next healthcheck after 4m.
# ~10 minutes later~
ops-bot: degraded: iowait still high, replica lag db-a-replica 22s now. reporting queries time out intermittently with 504s.
jin: looks like the slower pace still correlated with reporting job schedules. If we proceed we risk user-facing timeouts.
kari: decision: abort canary and roll back schema change (drop column). Jin, prepare revert. Also open follow-up: enforce pre-check for replica iowait and scheduled heavy jobs.
dba-bot: Revert plan: stop backfill-runner, run: ```ALTER TABLE transactions DROP COLUMN IF EXISTS normalized_amount;``` Note: DROP COLUMN on big table is fast in PG versions we run (metadata-only) but will require exclusive lock during drop in worst-case—we will do concurrent sequence: first ensure backfill jobs stopped and then drop.
deploybot: Executing rollback: stopping backfill-runner on db-a, scheduling DROP on primary, rollback started at ts=1709994005.
ops-bot: Post-rollback metrics (10m after): p50 write 21ms, p95 write 152ms, replica lag back to ~1s, reporting cluster errors cleared. No SEV.
jin: confirmed DROP executed and cluster returned to baseline. Opening PR with adjusted plan: add replica warm-up gate, preflight iowait check, and schedule backfill outside reporting windows.
kari: add this to release notes: "Canary aborted: normalized_amount backfill paused due to I/O and replica lag during reporting window. Will reattempt with stricter gating and lower concurrency. Follow-up INF-7801."
dba-bot: Ticket INF-7801 created and assigned to jin and kari.
ops-bot: Reminders added: update runbook with check steps and add native throttle for backfill-runner.
kari: Thanks all. We'll reconvene once PR lands and the backfill-runner supports run-time iowait gating. Closing thread.
